newsDocuments.headline: Gold slips as higher oil, US inflation data bolster Fed hike bets

segments.text: Gold prices slipped on Friday as higher oil prices and robust US inflation data strengthened the case for another Federal Reserve interest rate hike later this year.

“There were enough bullish indicators in the US macro data this week to keep the Fed on track for a potential December hike, which combined with oil at present levels means that gold continues to lose out from an inflation perspective.”
Oil prices rose on Friday and were set for a fourth monthly gain, as an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz highlighted supply risks stemming from the US-Israeli war on Iran.

newsDocuments.headline: Oil rises on supply concerns as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia

segments.text: SINGAPORE: Oil prices climbed in early trade on Friday on supply concerns after Yemen’s Houthis stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia , ​on track for a fourth straight monthly gain and the steepest ‌since July.
Brent crude futures rose 86 cents, or 0.75%, to $115.74 a barrel as of 0122 GMT.
US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose 72 cents, or 0.71%, to $102.72.
LONDON: Oil and gas giants Shell and TotalEnergies on Thursday reported soaring quarterly net profits as the Middle East war pushed up hydrocarbon prices — and the cost of living around the world.
Rising fossil fuel prices also saw Spanish oil group Repsol quadruple its net profit over the first nine months of the year, to 5 billion euros ($5.6 billion).
Energy majors are reaping bumper profits from disruptions to oil and gas supplies in the Middle East, pushing up refining margins and prices.

HOUSTON: Oil prices fell on Thursday in a choppy session as hopes for peace talks between the US and Iran offset some concerns over Middle East supply disruptions from an escalating regional conflict.
Brent crude futures settled down 44 cents, or 0.38 percent, to USD114.88 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures settled down 78 cents, or 0.76 percent, at USD102.
Both benchmarks fell by more than USD2 a barrel earlier in the session, unwinding some of Brent’s 1.3 percent and WTI’s 3 percent Wednesday gains.

newsDocuments.headline: Singapore oil product inventories edge up

segments.text: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil product inventories rose slightly over the week, government data showed on Thursday, led by higher clean distillate inventories.

Combined onshore oil product inventories at the key Asian fuel trading hub were at 38.49 million barrels in the week ended October 28, up 0.9 percent from the previous week, Enterprise Singapore data showed.
Traders are expecting more Northeast Asian exports of gasoil and diesel into November following a rare fourth batch of export quotas issued by China, as well as higher volumes from South Korea.
